source.docs: The repository is the source of truth. This catalog points at it; it never duplicates a procedure.
source.versions: compatibility/version-matrix.md — parsed at build time, so a version bump propagates without touching this file.
source.adr: decisions/ADR-*.md — the reasoning behind every option below.

methods.title: Bare metal
methods.summary: Physical servers, direct disks for Ceph and etcd, full control of PCIe and NUMA topology.
methods.bestFor: Ceph at scale, GPU inference, predictable IO latency, no hypervisor in the failure path.
requirements: IPMI or BMC access for out-of-band installation
Local SSD for etcd, dedicated NVMe for the Ceph OSD DB and WAL
RAID1 for the boot disk, or software RAID managed by the OS baseline

methods.title: Virtual machines
methods.bestFor: Small sites, lab and staging, environments without hardware.
requirements: Ceph OSD disks must be raw or SCSI-passthrough, never a shared virtual disk
etcd on a local SSD with dedicated vCPUs, never on shared storage
GPU needs passthrough; MIG is not virtualizable, so pass the whole card
The hypervisor joins the failure domain and must be in the DR plan

clusterMethods.title: Kubespray (Ansible)
clusterMethods.summary: Version-pinned inventory, idempotent, offline-capable, five releases supported in parallel.

options.title: Oracle Linux 8
options.warning: Kernel 4.18 is below the 4.19 recommendation in the Kubespray kernel matrix.

options.title: 5 control-plane nodes, stacked etcd
options.warning: Longer maintenance windows, and a third failure domain is needed to justify it.

options.title: Calico — mature, rich policy, IPIP/VXLAN
options.note: Calico is configured through the Kubespray inventory for the pinned release.

options.title: cephadm on dedicated hosts — Podman
options.note: Upstream default engine. No container engine dependency inside Kubernetes.

options.title: cephadm on dedicated hosts — Docker
options.warning: Supported but second-class upstream. Pull the engine from the internal mirror; docker.io on Ubuntu is too old.

options.title: HAProxy (L4, active health checks) + Nginx (L7, TLS), Keepalived, Docker Compose
Nginx only (L4 passthrough + L7), Keepalived, Docker Compose
F5 NGINX Gateway Fabric (Gateway API native)
Envoy Gateway (Gateway API native, second implementation)

components.title: Directory integration
components.note: Application-level only. Nodes are never joined to a directory. Keycloak brokers OIDC so each service speaks one dialect.

options.title: OpenBao (MPL 2.0)
options.note: The deployment model is portable from Vault. Use it when the BSL is not acceptable.

options.title: No central logging (not recommended for production)
Velero with CSI snapshots to object storage
Istio ambient (ztunnel per node, waypoints where L7 is needed)
options.note: Lower per-pod cost, but a ztunnel fault affects every pod on the node.

options.title: Istio sidecar (Envoy per pod)
options.warning: Adopt only when the threshold in service-mesh/evaluation.md is met. Adds a control plane and a failure domain.

options.title: GPU workers with MIG isolation and vLLM serving
GPU workers with time-slicing (development only, no VRAM isolation)
options.warning: No memory isolation between pods. Never for multi-tenant production.

steps.title: Confirm the requirements, assumptions and open decisions
actions: Close every open decision
Confirm the IP plan and the failure domains
Confirm the legal position on the Vault license

steps.title: Read the architecture and the decisions
actions: Review the architecture overview
Review the failure-domain table for the components you selected

steps.title: Stand up the internal repositories and mirror every artifact
actions: Deploy Harbor and Nexus
Mirror every artifact for the selected components
Verify offline install, image pull and chart deploy on a throwaway node

steps.title: DNS, NTP, network, PKI, load balancing
actions: Deploy DNS and NTP
Create the internal CA and distribute the trust bundle
Deploy the edge load balancer
Implement the firewall rules from the matrix

steps.title: Automation server, Ansible, AWX, GitLab, Vault
actions: Install Ansible in a virtualenv with the pinned version
Deploy AWX and register the runners
Deploy Vault on dedicated hosts and test the unseal procedure

steps.title: Provision and harden the nodes
actions: Configure the internal repositories
Apply sysctl, kernel modules and the security baseline
Confirm the local break-glass account and key work with no network dependency
Install the monitoring and logging agents

steps.title: Deploy the storage platform
actions: Create the CRUSH map with the host failure domain
Create the pools, the filesystem and the object store
Confirm Ceph HEALTH_OK before consuming any volume

steps.title: Deploy the application cluster with Kubespray
actions: Fill the inventory and the group vars from the generated files
Mirror the artifacts for the selected Kubespray release
Run cluster.yml, then validate the control plane and etcd

steps.title: CNI, ingress, load balancing, CSI
actions: Install the CNI and confirm kube-proxy replacement
Configure MetalLB and the ingress controller
Configure the CSI driver and the StorageClasses
Apply the Gateway API CRDs

steps.title: Deploy Istio and enable mTLS in stages
actions: Confirm the adoption threshold in service-mesh/evaluation.md is met
Extract and mirror every image the install and the dataplane need
Decide the dataplane mode: ambient (per node) or sidecar (per pod)
Install the control plane with Helm so Argo CD owns it
Apply PeerAuthentication STRICT to one namespace, watch metrics, then continue
Apply the default-deny AuthorizationPolicy only after the allow rules exist
Test a negative case: a pod that should be denied must be denied
Wire Istio telemetry into the existing Prometheus stack

steps.title: Rancher, Keycloak, Argo CD, backup
actions: Deploy the management cluster from its own inventory
Install Rancher and register the application cluster
Install Keycloak and wire OIDC for each service
Install Argo CD and sync the first application
Install Velero and run a first backup

steps.title: Integrate the directory at the application layer
actions: Confirm the break-glass local account works with the directory unreachable
Create a read-only bind account and store its credential in Vault
Configure Keycloak user federation first, read-only
Create one OIDC client per service with explicit redirect URIs
Wire services in order: Argo CD, Rancher, Harbor, GitLab, Vault, Kubernetes API
Remove the local superuser path only after a federated admin login is verified
Alert on failed federated logins and on a zero-login drop during working hours

steps.title: Vault integration, admission policy, runtime detection
actions: Bind the Vault role to the service account
Deploy the admission controllers in audit mode, then enforce
Enable the runtime detection ruleset
Verify certificate renewal and secret rotation

steps.title: Metrics, alerting, logs
actions: Install the monitoring stack and confirm every target is up
Configure the alert routes and the runbook links
Deploy the log pipeline and prove the redaction filter

steps.title: GPU workers, driver, sharing, serving
actions: Install the driver and the GPU Operator
Configure MIG and verify the isolation
Mirror the model weights and start the inference server
Validate the DCGM metrics

steps.title: Pipelines, approval gates, drift detection
actions: Wire the pipeline stages
Protect the branches and require the approvals
Turn on the nightly drift job

steps.title: Upgrades, backups, restore, disaster recovery
actions: Run the upgrade procedure on a staging copy
Restore into a scratch namespace and measure the RTO
Rebuild a node from the OS and Kubespray
Exercise the full rebuild order offline

steps.title: Acceptance tests and handover
actions: Execute every acceptance test and store the evidence
Record the known limitations
Hand over to the operations team

upgrades.title: Kubernetes and Kubespray
upgrades.downtime: Control plane rolls one node at a time. Workloads keep running if PodDisruptionBudgets exist; without them, expect pod restarts.
upgrades.rollback: None. Kubernetes does not support downgrade. The restore path is the backup taken in step 1.

steps.title: Confirm compatibility and mirror the target artifacts
actions: Target release is in the supported set (five releases, release-2.28 .. release-2.32)
Target Kubernetes minor is exactly one above the current one
Kubelet, kube-proxy, CoreDNS, etcd and the CNI versions are compatible with the target
Every image and binary for the target is mirrored and pull-verified
steps.command: python3 scripts/kubespray_release_matrix.py release-2.28 release-2.29 release-2.30 release-2.31 release-2.32

steps.title: Back up etcd and the cluster state
actions: Snapshot etcd on every control-plane node
Export the current inventory and group vars
Record the current versions for the rollback comparison
steps.command:
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
  snapshot save /backup/etcd-$(date +%F-%H%M).db

steps.title: Create the target release's environment
actions: Check out the target Kubespray release into its own directory
Create its own virtualenv with its pinned Ansible
Copy the inventory and re-apply the site group vars
Never reuse the previous release's virtualenv
steps.command:
git -C /opt/kubespray clone --branch release-2.32 --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray /opt/kubespray/release-2.32
python3 -m venv /opt/kubespray/venv-release-2.32
/opt/kubespray/venv-release-2.32/bin/pip install -r /opt/kubespray/release-2.32/requirements.txt

steps.title: Run the upgrade playbook
actions: Run cluster.yml from the target release against the existing inventory
Watch the control plane first, then the workers, one node at a time
Stop at the first failed task; do not re-run blindly

steps.title: Validate before moving the next minor
actions: All nodes report the target version and Ready
etcd members are healthy and the leader is stable
CNI and CoreDNS pods are running on the new version
A test workload schedules, pulls an image and answers a request
steps.command:
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl -n kube-system get pods
kubectl -n kube-system exec etcd-<node> -- etcdctl endpoint health --cluster

steps.title: Record the new binding
actions: Update the inventory's kubespray-release marker
Update the version matrix check date
Keep the previous release directory until the next upgrade succeeds

upgrades.title: Ceph (Rook or cephadm)
upgrades.downtime: No client downtime if the pools are healthy and one OSD at a time is drained.
upgrades.rollback: None across a major version. Downgrade within a minor is unsupported; the restore path is the backup.

steps.title: Health and capacity check
actions: ceph status is HEALTH_OK, not HEALTH_WARN
No degraded or backfilling placement groups
At least 25% free capacity in every pool
The Rook release supports the target Ceph version
steps.command:
ceph -s
ceph df
ceph osd tree

steps.title: Back up the cluster configuration
actions: Export the CRUSH map
Export the auth database
Snapshot the monitors' store (or the Rook config ConfigMap)
steps.command:
ceph osd getcrushmap -o /backup/crushmap.bin
ceph auth export -o /backup/auth.keyring
ceph config dump > /backup/ceph-config.json

steps.title: Upgrade the orchestrator first
actions: Rook: upgrade the operator, then CephCluster.spec.cephVersion
cephadm: run ceph orch upgrade start --ceph-version <target>
One daemon type at a time; wait for HEALTH_OK between types
steps.command:
helm upgrade rook-ceph rook-release/rook-ceph -n rook-ceph \
  --version {{version.rook}} -f values.yaml
kubectl -n rook-ceph patch cephcluster rook-ceph --type merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"cephVersion":{"image":"{{value.registryHost}}/ceph/ceph:{{version.ceph}}"}}}'

steps.title: Watch the daemons converge
actions: MONs first, then MGR, MDS, RGW, then OSDs
Do not start a second upgrade while a daemon is still restarting
Confirm each type reaches HEALTH_OK before the next
steps.command:
ceph orch ps --daemon-type mon
ceph orch ps --daemon-type osd
watch -n 10 ceph -s

steps.title: Prove the data path works
actions: Write and read a test object through RGW
Mount a CephFS volume and read a file
Create a PVC and confirm it binds
Run a CSI snapshot and restore
steps.command:
rados -p rbd bench 10 write --no-cleanup
kubectl -n {{value.appNamespace}} get pvc

upgrades.title: Istio
upgrades.downtime: No data-plane downtime with a revision-based canary. Sidecar mode restarts pods as namespaces move.
upgrades.rollback: Available only while the old revision is installed: move the namespace label back. No downgrade.

steps.title: Confirm the version window and mirror the images
actions: Target minor is one above the current one
The Kubernetes minor is inside the target Istio's support window
Every image for the new revision is mirrored
steps.command:
istioctl version
istioctl manifest generate --revision {{revision}} -f istio-operator.yaml | grep -E 'image: '

steps.title: Install the new revision alongside the old one
actions: Install with a revision name derived from the version
Both control planes run simultaneously
Do not remove the old revision yet
steps.command:
istioctl install --revision={{revision}} -f istio-operator.yaml
kubectl -n istio-system get pods -l istio.io/rev={{revision}}

steps.title: Move namespaces one at a time
actions: Change the injection label to the new revision
Restart the workloads in that namespace only
Watch error rate and latency for one business cycle before the next namespace
steps.command:
kubectl label namespace {{value.appNamespace}} istio.io/rev={{revision}} --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deployment -n {{value.appNamespace}}

steps.title: Prove mTLS and policy still apply
actions: istioctl analyze reports no errors
A negative authorization test is still denied
Proxy version matches the new revision
steps.command:
istioctl analyze -A
istioctl proxy-status

steps.title: Remove the old revision
actions: Only after every namespace has moved
Keep the old IstioOperator file in Git for reference
Record the new revision in the upgrade log
steps.command: istioctl uninstall --revision=<old-revision>

upgrades.title: Edge load balancer
upgrades.downtime: None if the VIP moves cleanly. One node at a time, draining first.
upgrades.rollback: Revert the image tag in the Compose file and recreate the stack on the same node.

steps.title: Confirm the standby can hold the VIP
actions: VRRP state on both nodes is BACKUP/MASTER as expected
Health checks are passing on both
The target image is mirrored and pullable

steps.title: Move traffic off one node
actions: Lower the VRRP priority or stop keepalived on the node being upgraded
Confirm the VIP moved and sessions drained
Upgrade the node that no longer holds the VIP
steps.command:
systemctl stop keepalived
ip -br addr show | grep {{value.edgeVip}} || echo 'VIP moved'

steps.title: Update the stack on that node
actions: Update the image tags in the Compose file
docker compose pull, then up -d
Confirm the health endpoint answers locally
steps.command:
cd /opt/edge && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://{{value.edgeVip}}/healthz

steps.title: Fail back and upgrade the second node
actions: Start keepalived on the first node and confirm it takes the VIP back
Repeat steps 2 and 3 on the second node
Both nodes end on the same image tag
steps.command:
systemctl start keepalived
ip -br addr show | grep {{value.edgeVip}}

steps.title: End-to-end check through the VIP
actions: TLS chain is valid through the VIP
Backend health is green in the stats page
VRRP state is stable with no flapping in the logs
steps.command:
curl -sSI https://{{value.edgeVip}}/ | head -3
journalctl -u keepalived --since '10 min ago' | grep -i state

upgrades.title: GPU operator, driver and CUDA
upgrades.downtime: The drained GPU node only. Inference capacity drops while the node is out.
upgrades.rollback: Reinstall the previous driver and operator versions on the drained node before uncordoning.

steps.title: Check the compatibility chain
actions: Driver branch supports the target CUDA
GPU Operator version supports the driver branch
Every image is mirrored
steps.command:
kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator
nvidia-smi

steps.title: Cordon and drain one GPU node
actions: Cordon the node
Drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-emptydir-data
Confirm no inference pod is still running there
steps.command:
kubectl cordon {{value.nodePrefix}}-gpu-1
kubectl drain {{value.nodePrefix}}-gpu-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

steps.title: Upgrade the operator, then the driver
actions: Upgrade the operator chart first
Let the operator roll the driver DaemonSet
Do not hand-install a driver on a node the operator manages
steps.command:
helm upgrade gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator -n gpu-operator \
  --version {{version.gpu-operator}} -f values.yaml
kubectl -n gpu-operator rollout status ds/nvidia-driver-daemonset

steps.title: Prove the node before uncordoning
actions: nvidia-smi shows the target driver and no Xid errors
A test pod requests a GPU and gets a MIG slice
DCGM metrics report for the node
steps.command:
kubectl uncordon {{value.nodePrefix}}-gpu-1
kubectl run gpu-test --image={{value.registryHost}}/platform/cuda-test --restart=Never --limits=nvidia.com/gpu=1

upgrades.title: Vault and the PKI
upgrades.downtime: None in an HA setup: upgrade the standby first, then fail over, then the old active.
upgrades.rollback: Restore the raft snapshot on the upgraded node. Vault does not support downgrade in place.

steps.title: Snapshot and confirm the unseal path
actions: Take a raft snapshot and verify it opens
Confirm the unseal keys are available offline
Confirm the audit device is writing
steps.command:
vault operator raft snapshot save /backup/vault-$(date +%F).snap
vault operator raft snapshot inspect /backup/vault-$(date +%F).snap

steps.title: Upgrade the standby node
actions: Stop the standby, upgrade the binary or image, start it
Confirm it rejoins as standby and the leader is unchanged
steps.command:
systemctl stop vault && <upgrade> && systemctl start vault
vault operator raft list-peers

steps.title: Step down and upgrade the old active
actions: Step down the active so the upgraded standby takes over
Upgrade the remaining node
Confirm the cluster has one leader and two followers
steps.command:
vault operator step-down
vault status

steps.title: Prove secrets, PKI and auth still work
actions: Read a secret through the Kubernetes auth method
Issue a certificate from the PKI mount
Log in through OIDC if it is enabled
Audit log shows the operations
steps.command:
vault kv get {{value.vaultEngine}}/apps/{{value.appNamespace}}/demo
vault write pki/issue/{{value.appNamespace}} common_name=test.{{value.domain}}

upgrades.title: Ingress controller portfolio
upgrades.downtime: None if traffic is migrated per hostname before the old controller is removed.
upgrades.rollback: Move the hostname back to the previous controller. Both remain installed until the migration is complete.

steps.title: Check the lifecycle stage and the deprecation date
actions: Controller is in Candidate, Supported or Deprecated
No upstream retirement announcement since the last check
The annotation set has a documented migration path
steps.command:
kubectl get ingressclass
kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=nginx-ingress

steps.title: Install the target controller in parallel
actions: Install with a distinct IngressClass or GatewayClass
Do not claim a hostname that the old controller still serves
Mirror the controller image and the CRDs
steps.command: kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/{{version.kubespray}}/standard-install.yaml

steps.title: Move one hostname at a time
actions: Create the equivalent Ingress or HTTPRoute on the new controller
Switch DNS or the edge upstream for that hostname only
Compare access logs and error rate for one business cycle
steps.command:
kubectl get httproute -A
curl -sSI https://app.{{value.domain}}/ | head -3

steps.title: Remove the old controller after the last hostname moves
actions: Confirm no IngressClass references remain
Remove the old controller and its CRDs
Update the ADR and the lifecycle table
steps.command:
kubectl get ingress -A -o wide
kubectl delete -f <old-controller-manifests>

upgrades.title: Helm 3 to Helm 4
upgrades.downtime: None. Helm is a client; the cluster is untouched by the client upgrade.
upgrades.rollback: Keep the Helm 3 binary and the release secrets. Helm 4 writes its own storage format; do not downgrade a release that Helm 4 already modified.

steps.title: Confirm the deadline and the chart compatibility
actions: Helm 3 security fixes end 2027-02-10
Kubespray release-2.32 ships Helm 3.22.0 internally: do not replace it inside the release venv
Every chart in use is tested under Helm 4
steps.command:
helm version
ls /opt/kubespray/release-2.32/bin/ 2>/dev/null | grep helm

steps.title: Install Helm 4 alongside Helm 3
actions: Install to a different path and name
Alias explicitly; never rely on PATH order for a migration
Argo CD keeps its own rendering path and is unaffected
steps.command:
curl -fsSL {{value.filesRepo}}/get.helm.sh/helm-v4-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz
install -m 0755 linux-amd64/helm /usr/local/bin/helm4

steps.title: Re-run every chart operation under Helm 4
actions: helm4 template for every chart, compare the manifests
helm4 list and helm4 get values in every namespace
Upgrade one non-critical release with helm4 and diff the result
steps.command:
helm4 list -A
helm4 template <release> <chart> -f values.yaml | diff - <(helm template <release> <chart> -f values.yaml)

steps.title: Switch the pipelines and keep Helm 3 until the date
actions: CI images use Helm 4
No release is operated by both binaries
Helm 3 binary stays available for one rollback window
steps.command:
helm4 version
helm4 list -A --all-namespaces | wc -l

# Generated by the cloud-native guide site
# Kubespray: {{choice.kubespray}}

kube_version: {{version.kubernetes}}
kube_network_plugin: {{choice.cni}}
kube_proxy_mode: ""
kube_pods_subnet: "{{value.podCidr}}"
kube_service_addresses: "{{value.serviceCidr}}"

github_url: "{{value.filesRepo}}/github.com"

exports.name: cephadm bootstrap script
exports.description: Prepares the engine and bootstraps the first monitor. Engine: {{choice.storage}}.
exports.template:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generated by the cloud-native guide site
# Engine: {{choice.storage}}   Ceph: {{version.ceph}}
# Hosts: {{cephHostList}}
set -euo pipefail

MON_IP="{{cephMonIp}}"
ENGINE="{{cephEngine}}"
REGISTRY="{{value.registryHost}}"

# 1. The container engine must exist before cephadm runs. cephadm will not install it.
if [ "$ENGINE" = "docker" ]; then
  dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io || \
    apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
  systemctl enable --now docker
  mkdir -p /etc/docker
  cat >/etc/docker/daemon.json <<EOF
{ "registry-mirrors": ["https://${REGISTRY}"], "live-restore": true }
EOF
  systemctl restart docker
else
  dnf install -y podman || apt-get install -y podman
  systemctl enable --now podman.socket
fi

# 2. cephadm itself.
dnf install -y cephadm || apt-get install -y cephadm

# 3. Bootstrap. --docker is passed only for the Docker engine.
cephadm {{cephEngineFlag}} bootstrap \
  --mon-ip "$MON_IP" \
  --cluster-network {{value.storageCidr}} \
  --registry "$REGISTRY" \
  --log-to-file

# 4. Copy the config and keyring to the other hosts, then add them.
#    for h in {{cephOtherIps}}; do ssh root@$h mkdir -p /etc/ceph; \
#      scp /etc/ceph/ceph.conf /etc/ceph/ceph.client.admin.keyring root@$h:/etc/ceph/; done
cephadm shell -- ceph -s

# Generated by the cloud-native guide site
# Dataplane: {{choice.edge}}
name: edge

services:
  haproxy:
    image: {{value.registryHost}}/edge/haproxy:{{version.haproxy}}
    container_name: edge-haproxy
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped

      retries: 3
    sysctls:
      net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind: "1"

  nginx:
    image: {{value.registryHost}}/edge/nginx:{{version.nginx}}
    container_name: edge-nginx
    network_mode: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "nginx", "-t"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
    sysctls:
      net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind: "1"

  keepalived:

    pid: host
    sysctls:
      net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind: "1"

exports.name: Edge node bootstrap script
exports.description: Kernel settings, directories, images and stack start. Run on every edge node.
exports.template:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generated by the cloud-native guide site
# Edge nodes: {{edgeHostList}}   VIP: {{value.edgeVip}}
set -euo pipefail

REGISTRY="{{value.registryAddr}}"
STACK_DIR=/opt/edge

# 1. Non-local bind, so the dataplane can listen on the VIP before it moves.
cat >/etc/sysctl.d/90-edge.conf <<'EOF'
net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind = 1
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
EOF
sysctl --system

# 2. Firewall: unicast VRRP, no multicast.
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule protocol value="vrrp" accept' || true
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8404/tcp || true
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8443/tcp || true
firewall-cmd --reload || true

# 3. Runtime from the internal mirror, never from the internet.
dnf install -y docker-ce docker-compose-plugin || \
  apt-get install -y docker.io docker-compose-v2
systemctl enable --now docker

# 4. Stack directory and the generated files.
install -d -m 0750 "$STACK_DIR" "$STACK_DIR/certs" "$STACK_DIR/keepalived.d"
# Copy docker-compose.yml, haproxy.cfg, nginx.conf, keepalived.conf and
# keepalived.d/* into $STACK_DIR before starting the stack.

# 5. Start and verify.
cd "$STACK_DIR"
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w 'edge health: %{http_code}\n' https://{{value.edgeVip}}/healthz || true

exports.name: Kubespray run script
exports.description: Runs the pinned release from its own checkout and virtualenv, offline.
exports.template:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generated by the cloud-native guide site
# Release: {{choice.kubespray}}   Kubernetes: {{version.kubernetes}}
set -euo pipefail

RELEASE="{{choice.kubespray}}"
BASE=/opt/kubespray
SRC="$BASE/$RELEASE"
INV="$BASE/inventory/{{value.clusterName}}-{{value.env}}"

# One checkout and one virtualenv per release. The Ansible and Python pins differ.
test -d "$SRC" || { echo "missing checkout: $SRC"; exit 1; }
test -d "$INV" || { echo "missing inventory: $INV"; exit 1; }

cd "$SRC"
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source "$BASE/venv-$RELEASE/bin/activate"
ansible --version

ansible-playbook -i "$INV/hosts.ini" cluster.yml \
  -b --become-user=root \
  -e @"$INV/group_vars/all/offline.yml" \
  -e kube_version="{{version.kubernetes}}" \
  "$@"

kubectl --kubeconfig "$INV/artifacts/admin.conf" get nodes -o wide
kubectl --kubeconfig "$INV/artifacts/admin.conf" -n kube-system get pods

exports.name: mTLS and authorization policies
exports.description: STRICT mTLS per namespace, default deny, and the allow rules. Apply deny only after the allows exist.
exports.template:
# Generated by the cloud-native guide site
# Namespace: {{value.appNamespace}}
# Stage 1: install defaults to permissive. Move one namespace at a time.
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: {{value.appNamespace}}
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
---
# Stage 2: default deny. Apply only after the allow rules below exist.
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: {{value.appNamespace}}
spec: {}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-same-namespace
  namespace: {{value.appNamespace}}
spec:
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from:
        - source:
            namespaces: ["{{value.appNamespace}}"]
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-ingress
  namespace: {{value.appNamespace}}
spec:
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from:
        - source:
            namespaces: ["istio-ingress"]

exports.description: One GatewayClass claim per hostname. Do not put this in front of a hostname another controller serves.

kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: istio-gateway
  namespace: istio-ingress
spec:

  parentRefs:

  rules:
    - matches:

        - name: app

exports.description: Application-level only. Nodes are never joined to a directory (ADR-0015).

# Directory integration — {{value.clusterName}} ({{value.env}})

Directory: `{{value.directoryHost}}`
Base DN: `{{value.directoryBaseDn}}`
OIDC issuer: `{{value.keycloakHost}}/realms/platform`

**Scope: application layer only.** No SSSD, realmd, Kerberos membership or AD join on any Linux
node. Local break-glass account and offline key are the node recovery path.

## Selected integrations

{{idpTargets}}

## Order of work

1. Confirm the break-glass local account works with the directory unreachable.
2. Create a read-only bind account; store its credential in Vault, never in Git.
3. Configure Keycloak user federation first, `editMode=READ_ONLY`.
4. Create one OIDC client per service, explicit redirect URI, no wildcard.
5. Wire services in order: Argo CD, Rancher, Harbor, GitLab, Vault, Kubernetes API.
6. Remove each service's local superuser path only after a federated admin login works.
7. Alert on failed federated logins, bind failures, and a zero-login drop in working hours.

## Group → role mapping

| Group (DN) | Service | Role |
|---|---|---|
| CN=platform-admins | all | platform administrator |
| CN=platform-operators | Rancher, Argo CD | operator, sync |
| CN=platform-viewers | all | read-only |

Reference: `identity/directory-integration.md`
